general_information.Description: A- Listening: Upon completion of the course, students should be able to - Listen to talk shows or radio shows to identify main ideas (U1) - Listen for rhetorical questions via an invention description (U2) - Listen to radio news programs or reports to look for bias (U2), reasons and explanations (U3), summaries (U3) , or listen to understand a sequence of events (U4) - Listen to lectures for similarities and differences (U5), for supporting statements (U5), or listen to know phrases used to introduce examples (U1) - Listen to a presentation for organization cues to distinguish facts and opinions (U4) B- Speaking: Upon completion of the course, students should be able to - Use appropriate language to let other people know that they are paying attention and that they are interested in what people are saying during a conversation or informal discussion (U1) - Give examples to express ideas clearly and convincingly (U2) - Give reasons to contribute to an academic discussion (U3) - Change and return to topics in a conversation (U4) - Interrupt politely during a lecture or a classroom discussion to understand it clearly (U5) - Pronounce correctly thought groups (know how to pause correctly) (U1) and weak forms of ‘that’ and ‘as’ (U2) - Use appropriate language express disagreement politely (U3) - Know and use intonation patterns in questions and to express feelings and attitudes (U4) - Stress correctly to express the right meanings and to emphasize important information (U5) - Introduce themselves (U1) - Discuss the result of an experiment, research findings and applications, and water issues (U3) - Present the pros and cons of an invention; about a city, a plan for a public space, future problems and personal and community values. (U2, U5) - debate an argument.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend more than 80% of in-class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfil tasks given by intructor after class - Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes - Use CD-ROM provided with the textbook - Access the course website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Use appropriate language to let other people know that they are paying attention and that they are interested in what people are saying during a conversation or informal discussion.
Give examples to express ideas clearly and convincingly and reasons to contribute to an academic discussion.
Change and return to topics in a conversation and interrupt politely during a lecture or a classroom discussion to understand it clearly.
Use appropriate language express disagreement politely and know and use intonation patterns in questions and to express feelings and attitudes.
Listen to talk shows or radio shows to identify main ideas.

Listen for rhetorical questions via an invention description, and listen to radio news programs or reports to look for bias, reasons and explanations, summaries, or listen to understand a sequence of events.
Listen to lectures for similarities and differences, for supporting statements, or listen to know phrases used to introduce examples.
Listen to a presentation for organization cues to distinguish facts and opinions.
